sample_unit: clinical ethics scenarios (each tested with 53 socio-demographic modifiers, 10 repeats, nine LLMs; ~0.5M prompts)
models_evaluated: nine LLMs (not named in the text)

links.outcome: Change in LLM ethical choices when patient socio-demographic modifiers were added to prompts
links.effect: All nine models altered responses when given socio-demographic details (p<0.001). High-income modifiers increased utilitarian choices and lowered beneficence and nonmaleficence; marginalized-group modifiers raised autonomy. No model was consistent across all scenarios.
links.quote: All models altered their responses when introduced with socio-demographic details (p<0.001).

screen.reason: The study benchmarks the impact of socio-demographic modifiers on ethical decision-making across nine LLMs using synthetic clinical scenarios, without testing an organizational deployment safeguard or practice.
